title: Ball goes wide: take the half-space
titleKid: Ball wide? Find the in-between strip
brief: Your #6 plays the ball out to your full-back, who has space to run up the touchline.
briefKid: Your midfielder passes out wide to your defender, who has space to run.
question: The ball is out wide on your side. Where do you go?
questionKid: The ball is out wide near you. Where do you go?

takeaway.standard: With the ball wide, get into the ball-side half-space between their midfield and back line: their full-back and centre-back must decide who takes you, and either choice opens a pass.
takeaway.kid: Ball out wide? Find the gap between the wing and the middle, behind their midfielders.

misconceptions.text: You stayed in the middle next to your #6, so their midfield can cover you both and the full-back has no pass inside.
misconceptions.textKid: You stayed in the middle. Move toward the ball, into the channel behind their midfielders.

misconceptions.text: You dropped behind the ball on the same flank, which is a safe pass but beats nobody; get ahead of their midfield in the half-space.
misconceptions.textKid: You went behind the ball. Get ahead, behind their midfielders.

notes: Authored answer (engine disagreement). With the ball wide on the #8's side, layer A (HELIOS) drags the ball-side #8 into the wing lane 5-10 m inside and behind the ball, in front of their midfield line: base (54.5, 56.2). In engine mode the ghost is (49.5, 55.2) scoring 87 (A) with between-lines 0.00, occupancy 0.60 and support-distance 0.65: a deep support spot behind the ball, not P1. P1 has no rule of its own (its ruleIds are empty), so the zone is centred on the ball-side half-space pocket between their #6/#8 and their centre-back/full-back, with a tighter tolerance (4 x 3 m) so the ghost search does not drift into the wing lane, where their #8 follows the learner (scene.js settle) and the spot is judged 84 in the drill frame. The rules agree at the ideal (ghost 96: between-lines 1.00, lane-open 1.00; the support angle with the #9 is 0.65). The #9 is keyed on their centre-back's shoulder in the centre lane, as in the P1 picture (he pins the centre-back so the half-space stays free).
